criteria.text: The participant is over 70 years of age
The participant has a historically or pathologically confirmed diagnosis of metastatic Stage IV NSCLC without EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 genomic alterations.

The participant has actionable mutations (other than EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 genomic alterations) and has received 1 additional line of therapy with the appropriate health authority approved targeted therapy.
The participant has documented radiographic disease progression on or after the first-line therapy, including concurrent or sequential ICI and platinum-based chemotherapy ± bevacizumab.

The participant has received no more than 1 prior line of therapy if ICI and platinum-based chemotherapy were administered concurrently, and no more than 2 prior lines of therapy for sequential administration of platinum-based chemotherapy and ICI as 2 separate lines.

The participant has residual resectable disease after completion of the platinum-based chemotherapy component of the front-line ICI and platinum-based chemotherapy combination, meets all eligibility criteria except documented disease progression, and intends to receive TIL therapy after disease progression.

Prior systemic therapy in the adjuvant or neoadjuvant setting, or as part of definitive chemoradiotherapy, counts as a line of therapy if the patient had disease progression during or within 12 months after the completion of such therapy.
The participant has at least 1 resectable lesion for TIL production and at least one remaining measurable lesion, as defined by RECIST v1.1.
The participant has adequate organ function.
The participant has an LVEF > 45% and NYHA Class 1.
The participant has adequate pulmonary function.
The participant has an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.

The participant is of childbearing potential or has a partner of childbearing potential and is willing to practice an approved method of highly effective birth control during treatment and up to 12 months after all protocol-related therapy.
The participant has EGFR, ALK or ROS1 driver mutations.
The participant has symptomatic, untreated brain metastases.
The participant has had an allogeneic organ transplant or prior cell therapy within the past 20 years.
The participant has any form of primary immunodeficiency.
The participant is on systemic steroid therapy ≥ 10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent.
The participant has received a live or attenuated vaccination within 28 days prior to the start of treatment.
The participant has had another primary malignancy within the previous 3 years.
The participant is participating in another interventional clinical study within 21 days.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Autologous LN-145 in Patients With Metastatic Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer". Your earlier answers already covered 6 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you over 70 years of age?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, no dear, I'm 67. I'm not quite there yet!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received 1 additional line of therapy with a targeted treatment approved by your health authority for a mutation other than EGFR, ALK, or ROS1?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any of those targeted pills. I just had the chemo and the immune therapy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. After your first treatment (chemo and immune therapy), did your cancer grow or spread again on a scan?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh yes, it did. The Tecentriq stopped working and the cancer grew again, that's why I'm looking at this trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. After your chemo and immunotherapy, did your doctor say you still have cancer that can be surgically removed?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, no dear. It's spread to my liver and lymph nodes, so there's no way they could take it all out with surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent blood tests or organ function checks in the last 2 weeks to make sure your body is ready for treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I'm not sure about that one, dear. I don't keep track of exactly when my last blood work was done.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a recent heart function test (like an echocardiogram) to check your heart's pumping strength?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had that. I know my heart is okay generally, but I don't think they did a pumping strength test recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, have you had an echocardiogram (a heart ultrasound) in the last 2 weeks to check your heart's pumping strength?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had an echocardiogram in the last two weeks. I know my heart is fine, but I don't think they did that specific test recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent lung function tests (like spirometry) to check how well your lungs are working?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I wouldn't know that, dear. I'm not sure if they did any of those lung function tests recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently using a highly effective birth control method, or do you have a partner who is using one, to prevent pregnancy during the study and for 12 months after treatment ends?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh heavens, no, I'm 67 years old. I'm certainly not pregnant or breastfeeding, so that's not a worry for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been tested for EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 mutations in your lung cancer? These are specific genetic changes in the tumor cells.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I wouldn't know that, dear. I don't keep track of those specific genetic test results.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received an organ transplant from another person, or had any prior cell therapy treatments in the last 20 years?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had an organ transplant. Just this one cancer, nothing else.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a primary immunodeficiency, which is a condition where your immune system doesn't work properly from birth?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know what that means, dear. I've never heard of a primary immunodeficiency. I just know I have this lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, have you ever been told by a doctor that you have a condition where your immune system doesn't work properly from birth, or have you had frequent, severe infections since childhood?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know, honey. I've never been told I have a condition where my immune system doesn't work properly from birth, and I don't recall having frequent severe infections since I was a child.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking prednisone or a similar steroid medicine at a dose of 10 mg per day or more?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I take a little white pill in the morning, but I'm not sure what it is, so I don't know if it's prednisone or how much it is.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Could you check the bottle or box for the name of the pill and the strength (mg)? Or do you know if it's a steroid like prednisone?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, dear, but I really don't know what that little white pill is called or how strong it is. I just take it in the morning and hope for the best.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any live or attenuated vaccines (like MMR, varicella, or the nasal flu spray) in the last 28 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know, honey. I'm not sure if I've had any of those live vaccines recently. I just get my regular shots when the doctor says so.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you joined or started any other clinical trial studies in the last 21 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't joined any other studies recently. I'm just looking into this one.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.

The message claims the person knows their heart is fine, which contradicts the fact that they only stated they have not had a recent heart attack, stroke, or heart failure requiring hospital care, without asserting their heart is currently fine or that they know its status.

The message asserts that the person has never been told they have a primary immunodeficiency and recalls no frequent severe infections, which introduces specific medical history details not present in the provided facts.

The message asserts information about the person's vaccination history (live vaccines), which is not mentioned in the facts and contradicts the persona's tendency to claim ignorance about specific medical details or stick to the provided facts.
